When you join GDIT, you’re stepping into an environment where your creative contributions and ideas truly matter. You’ll be part of a forward-thinking team dedicated to crafting impactful messaging and designs that enable our mission to solve the world’s toughest challenges. Explore a career at GDIT and you’ll find endless opportunities to grow alongside colleagues who share your sense of ownership and pride in the meaningful work we do.

Job Description:

Electronics Technician Maintenance III

GDIT is seeking qualified candidates for Electronics Technician Maintenance III in support of the Warfighter Training Readiness Solution (W-TRS) Contract, formally known as ATMP.

W-TRS program purpose is to provide ongoing Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and training-related services in support of U.S. Army training and the U.S. Army SC mission. Services include program management, O&M of Training Aids, Devices, Simulators and Simulations (TADSS) and Government Furnished Property (GFP), TADSS-related services, training services (e.g., individual, crew, unit, and collective training support programs), and logistics services.

GDITs ETM III Long Bow Training Aircraft Survivability Equipment Simulation Suite (LB TASS) Contact Team (CT) Member will report to the site lead as our Subject Matter Expert (SME) for ensuring Army standard of maintenance for sequential installation, testing, removing and maintaining Threat-Integrated Air Defense Systems (T-IADS) kits and equipment for the Army aviation fleet

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact as an ETM III. Here, you’ll tailor cutting-edge solutions to the unique requirements of our customer. GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career.

At GDIT, people are our differentiators. As an ETM III you will help ensure today is safe and tomorrow is smarter. Our work depends on a Team Lead joining our team to help build and enable the readiness of our Nation's Army!

HOW AN ELECTRONICS TECHNICIAN MAINTENANCE III MAKE AN IMPACT:

  • Installation, testing, removing and maintaining Threat-Integrated Air Defense Systems (T-IADS) kits and equipment for the Army aviation fleet.

  • Performs routine and advanced tasks troubleshooting and repairing military simulators, including using tools and test equipment such as multimeters to diagnose faults. Replace components, wiring circuits, and complex repair functions.

  • Travel (TDY) to numerous locations (CONUS & OCONUS) to support the Army Aviation fleet training.

  • Applies routine advanced technical knowledge and troubleshooting procedures to solve routine problems that typically can be solved by reference to manufacturers’ manuals or similar documents; applies skills in restoring equipment operations.

  • On-site maintenance performed In Accordance With (IAW) technical data; if technical data/checklist is not provided for any single item, maintenance IAW the best commercial standards. Maintain all the documentation (Operator & Maintainer Manual, Instructor/Operator Manual, Commercial Off- The-Shelf Manual, Technical Data Package Schematics and Cold Start Procedures) spares and tools.

  • Captures and records accurate and timely maintenance history ensuring that unique corrective measures for work orders and repair are annotated into the Management Information System (MIS).

  • Reports maintenance issues and general operations updates with supervisor.

  • Maintain all GFP hardware and software IAW technical manuals, including, but not limited to, commercial software installation and Government provided installation (patches, updates).

  • Report on acquisition of supplies, equipment, and parts weekly to supervise.

  • Conduct an inspection and inventory of all assigned equipment before and after each live fire-training event for accountability and serviceability.

  • Supports the required GDIT/W-TRS cross training plan to support other W-TRS TADSS on installation.

  • May supervise junior technicians when required.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

  • Education: AA or 3 years equivalent

  • Required Experience: 3+ years of related experience Maintaining US Army TADSS and/or Military experience preferred

  • Security Clearance: None

  • Experience using technical manuals, schematics and drawings.

  • Ability to learn the W-TRS Management Information System (MIS) for controls/recording all work orders and Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) property control

  • Required Skills and Abilities: Superb communication skills. Ability to supervise junior technicians when requested or required.

  • Must be able to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and be able to lift a maximum of 50 lbs.

  • Must be able to obtain/maintain a valid state driver’s license and post driving privileges

  • Must be able to obtain a passport and travel visas for OCNUS travel when requested.

  • Location: On Customer Site and other military reservations

  • Must be able to travel up to 75% of the time.

Recognized as one of America’s Best-In-State Employers for 2024, the City of Virginia Beach is proud to offer a diverse and dynamic work environment. Our workforce plays a crucial role in delivering exceptional government services to both our citizens and fellow City employees. Apply now to join an organization where you truly make a difference.

Job Duties and Preferred Qualifications:

The Virginia Beach Human Services Department is seeking candidates for the position of Human Services Supervisor I (HSSI) in the Permanency Programs Unit. The Permanency program includes Foster Care and Adoptions Programs. This position provides direct supervision for Family Services Specialist assigned to the Foster Care.

Duties:

  • After normal business hours Foster Care supervisory coverage on a rotating basis.

  • Provide supportive supervision for family services specialist staff members assigned to permanency programs.

  • Provide supervision for a minimum of five Family Services Specialist.

  • Daily leadership, supervision, direction, planning, monitoring, and evaluation of work activities and caseload assignments in the Foster Care program.

  • Supervise the foster care cases from intake through reunification or adoption.

  • Ensure that Family Services Specialist engage families from a strengths-based perspective with an emphasis on family engagement and working towards reunification and permanency.

  • Utilize Safe Measures to monitor case work activities throughout the life of a case.

  • Utilizes OASIS database to review case records, ensuring that appropriate services and treatment are provided to youth and documented accordingly.

  • Participates in professional interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary treatment team meetings.

  • Assist with the development and training of department staff on client service planning.

  • Facilitate family team meetings to build a positive rapport with the children and families.

  • Monitor case work activities to ensure that foster care plans are based on the individual strengths and needs of each family and child.

  • Responsible for hiring and performing annual performance appraisals for all positions under supervision.

  • Lead and/or participate in state, regional, and community initiatives as requested.

  • Promote awareness of HSD programs in the community.

  • Follow federal, state, and local guidelines associated with child safety, well-being, and permanency.

  • Provide after normal business hours foster care services on a rotating basis.

  • Assist social work team members in the community as needed.

  • Records management to ensure that cases are documented within 24 hours and referrals are closed within program procedures and guidelines.

  • Assist in continuous quality improvement reviews and data collection.

  • Collect, evaluate, and analyze program data and provide recommendations to department leadership through timely reports.

Work Schedule: Monday – Friday 8:30am – 5:30pm

And here's the exciting part - the selected candidate will qualify for a $3,000 hiring bonus!

Hiring bonuses shall only be for new hires of original employment or reemployment as defined in Human Resources Policy No. 5.0.

  • Master’s Degree in Human Services Field or Equivalent

  • Foster Care Supervisory Experience

  • Practical Foster Care Case Management Experience

  • Experience in Social Work or Human Services

  • Data Driven Decision-Making Skills

  • Utilization of Outcome Measures and Data Collection Tools for Quality Assurance

  • Mental Health, Substance Abuse, or Child Development Training

title: Substitute Youth Development Professional (After-School)
company: Boys & Girls Clubs of San Leandro
description:
Title: Substitute Youth Development Professional (Sub-YDP)
Organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of San Leandro
Location: San Leandro, CA / San Lorenzo, CA / Union City, CA
Department: Programs

Reports to: Program Manager

Direct Reports: None

Exempt Status: Non-Exempt

Position Type: Part-Time, On-Site

Compensation: $25-$30/hr.

Benefits: Paid Sick-Leave, EAP, Calm, Paid Holidays

About the role:


As a Substitute Youth Development Professional (Sub-YDP) you'll have the opportunity to directly contribute to Boys and Girls Clubs of San Leandro. You'll be fostering a safe and enriching space that promotes curiosity, creativity, and positive relationships. What makes this role unique is the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in early childhood development, work with a diverse and supportive team, and make a lasting impact during one of the most critical stages of a child’s growth.


As a Sub YDP, you’ll step into a variety of vibrant after-school environments filled with creativity, play, and growth. You’ll lead fun, hands-on activities, encourage positive relationships, and help kids develop social-emotional skills; all while working with a supportive, diverse team that values your contribution.


Why you’ll love this role:

  • Flexibility: Work when it fits your schedule across multiple school sites (We serve the San Lorenzo, San Leandro, and New Haven Unified School Districts).
  • Impact: Every day you work, you’re shaping young minds and making a difference.
  • Experience: Gain valuable skills in youth development and education.
  • Community: Be part of a mission-driven organization that cares about kids and families.

What you need: A positive attitude, reliable transportation, and the ability to adapt to different locations within the San Lorenzo, San Leandro, and New Haven Unified School Districts.


Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions:

Program and Operations Support

  • Supervision & Safety: Ensure a safe and nurturing environment for youth participants.
  • Program Facilitation: Lead engaging after-school programs and activities for a group of approximately 20 students.
  • Lesson Planning: Facilitate lesson plans and activities that promote personal growth, educational achievement, and character development.

Classroom Management and Teaching

  • Establish classroom rules and behavior.
  • Provide for children's basic needs and ensure supervision.
  • Adapt teaching methods to children's interests and learning styles.
  • Manage classroom activities, lessons, play, breaks, and meals.
  • Track children's progress and communicate effectively with parents and teachers.
  • Maintain a clean and organized classroom.

Relationships

  • Mentoring: Serve as a positive role model and mentor to young participants, fostering their self-esteem and personal development.
  • Maintaining a Positive Environment: Cultivate a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere where every child feels valued and respected.
  • Team Collaboration: Collaborate with colleagues to ensure program goals are met and share best practices.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Southlake, Texas.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Southlake area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Southlake requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Funktionsdirektør til Performance, Kvalitet og Risiko i Erhverv og Kapitalmarked
description:
Vil du være med til at skabe opfølgning, overblik og solide beslutningsgrundlag for ledelsen i et af bankens største forretningsområder?

Til Erhverv og Kapitalmarked søger vi en systematisk og forretningsorienteret profil, der kan kombinere data og komplekse problemstillinger til indsigter, der understøtter beslutninger og udviklingen af forretningen.

Du får en central rolle med stor berøringsflade på tværs af banken og bliver en vigtig sparringspartner for ledelsen i arbejdet med performance, rentabilitet, risiko, governance og compliance.

Om rollen

Som ansvarlig for Performance, Kvalitet og Risiko er du med til at skabe et ensartet og tværgående fundament for styring og opfølgning i Erhverv og Kapitalmarked. Du bidrager til at sikre, at ledelsen har det nødvendige indblik i resultater, risici og potentialer på tværs af ressortet.

Dine opgaver vil blandt andet være at:

  • skabe grundlag for ensartet synliggørelse af performance og økonomisk transparens på tværs af Erhverv og Kapitalmarked
  • understøtte ledelsen med analyser, opfølgning og beslutningsgrundlag vedrørende produkter, indsatser, rentabilitet og øvrige forretningsmæssige målepunkter
  • identificere afvigelser og forbedringspotentialer samt bidrage med anbefalinger til handling
  • bidrage til prognoser, budgetopfølgning og ensartet opfølgning på centrale styringsparametre i samarbejde med relevante interessenter
  • fungere som bindeled mellem forretningen og centrale samarbejdspartnere inden for blandt andet økonomi, risiko, compliance og udvikling
  • følge op på risiko- og complianceområdet, herunder rapportering og indsatser relateret til governance og datakvalitet
  • understøtte arbejdet med at sikre høj kvalitet i processer, styring og efterlevelse af interne politikker og eksterne krav

Din profil

Du trives med at bevæge dig fra rapporter og data til indsigter og beslutningsstøtte og du kan skabe sammenhæng mellem økonomi, performance og forretningsmæssige prioriteringer.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • har en relevant videregående uddannelse, f.eks. cand.merc., cand.oecon., cand.scient.pol. eller tilsvarende
  • har erfaring med analyse, økonomi, performanceopfølgning eller business controlling
  • kan omsætte komplekse data til klare konklusioner og handlingsorienterede anbefalinger
  • arbejder struktureret og trives med at skabe overblik på tværs af mange interessenter
  • motiveres af at understøtte ledelsesbeslutninger og skabe værdi gennem indsigt og analyse
  • kan navigere i komplekse problemstillinger inden for f.eks. økonomi, risiko, compliance eller governance
  • formår at skabe relationer og samarbejde på tværs af fagområder og organisatoriske enheder
  • kommunikerer klart og tydeligt til både ledere og specialister

Om funktionen

Du bliver ansvarlig for funktionen Performance, Kvalitet og Risiko med reference til bankdirektør Erik Gadeberg og understøtter ledelsen i Erhverv og Kapitalmarked med analyser, styring, governance og opfølgning. Funktionen bidrager til at skabe sammenhæng mellem bankens strategi, økonomi og de enkelte forretningsområders mål og resultater.

Vi samarbejder tæt med blandt andet Strategi og kunderejser, Økonomi, Risiko, Compliance, Udvikling og de forretningsvendte enheder og lægger vægt på høj faglighed, ordentlighed og et godt samarbejde.

Du får en hverdag med stor variation, betydeligt ansvar og gode muligheder for at bidrage til både opgaver og løsninger.

Arbejdssted er primært Silkeborg med forventning om fysisk tilstedeværelse i København efter behov.

Ansøgning

Vi oplever mangfoldighed som en ressource i vores opgaveløsning og i vores fællesskab. Derfor opfordrer vi alle til at søge – vi ser frem til at modtage din ansøgning, hvor du beskriver netop dine evner og motivation i forhold til jobbet.

Lead HR Business Partner Line Højer Fogde varetager din ansøgning.

description:

The Zonal Coordinator (ZC) holds the fourth cadre of leadership within the Harvesters Small Groups system. The ZC oversees the administration and spiritual health of the cluster of cells within an assigned Zone (defined by geography or interest group), ensuring alignment with the vision, mission, and strategic goals of the church's cell ministry.


QUALITIES TO CONSIDER

•Committed to the study of the Word and to a consistent life of prayer.

•Partly employed or running a profitable business.

•A member of the church; may be new to the cell system.

•Demonstrated track record of obedience and alignment to the vision and statutes of the Harvesters Small Group Community.

•Demonstrated track record of integrity amongst members.

•Evident leadership skill and capacity to develop others.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Leadership & Administration

•Oversee and ensure implementation of organizational policies and small-group strategic initiatives within the Zone.

•Organize and coordinate regular zonal meetings, training sessions, and leadership development activities.

•Submit weekly KRA reports and conduct weekly one-on-one performance reviews with Cell Leaders.

Spiritual Oversight & Pastoral Care

•Provide pastoral support to cell leaders and members within the Zone.

•Facilitate mentorship, discipleship, and “Next Step” conversations to deepen spiritual growth.

•Mobilize members to daily morning prayers/devotionals and weekly Zonal Prayers, driving strong participation among leaders and members.

•Encourage unity, cooperation, and sound doctrine among zonal leaders.

Leader & Volunteer Development

•Identify, train, and mentor cell leaders and volunteers to improve effectiveness and readiness for role assignment.

•Drive weekly outline reviews, monthly podcast distribution/review, and informal one-on-one training with leaders.

•Support recruitment and onboarding of new leaders and volunteers within the Zone.

Growth, Care & Assimilation

•Drive new cell growth and maintain healthy average cell attendance.

•Conduct weekly one-on-one engagement with leaders and monthly membership calls to strengthen assimilation.

•Apply the Pastoral Care Standard for celebrations and member support.

Community Engagement & Conflict Resolution

•Represent the Zone/church at community events and outreach initiatives.

•Mediate conflicts among leaders or members, escalating appropriately and applying disciplinary guidance in line with church policy.

•Support crisis-response efforts affecting members within the Zone.



Requirements

  • Prior leadership experience in a faith-based, ministry, or nonprofit setting is an advantage; new entrants to the cell system with strong leadership potential may be considered.

  • Working knowledge of, and demonstrated alignment with, the Harvesters Small Group Community vision and statutes.

  • Experience mentoring or developing others is preferred.

title: Minor Works Project Manager
description:
Summary:

Do you want a role where your expertise in project delivery and contract management truly matters?

We're looking for an experienced and proactive Project Manager to join our team and drive the successful delivery of a diverse portfolio of essential minor works projects. This is a brilliant opportunity to apply your skills across vital infrastructure, from treatment works upgrades and pipeline installations to reservoir maintenance and pumping station improvements.

If you're a seasoned professional looking for meaningful work and ready for your next big challenge, this exciting role offers autonomy, complexity, and clear purpose.

Main Responsibilities:

You will be responsible for the safe and successful delivery of your project portfolio to Time, Cost, and Quality. Key responsibilities include:

  • Project Delivery: Managing the full project lifecycle—initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, control, and closure—for assigned clean water infrastructure projects.

  • Contract Management (NEC Focus): Leading the administration of contracts, primarily under the NEC3/NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) framework. This includes managing contract award, proactively handling communication, compensation events, early warnings, programme submissions, payments, and dispute resolution in line with NEC procedures.

  • Scope & Schedule Management: Defining project scope and deliverables, developing detailed project schedules, tracking progress, and implementing corrective actions.

  • Budget & Cost Control: Developing project budgets, monitoring expenditure, forecasting costs, and managing financial performance.

  • Risk & Opportunity Management: Identifying, assessing, and mitigating project risks, proactively managing the early warning process, and identifying opportunities for project enhancement.

  • Stakeholder Engagement: Liaising effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including operations teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory bodies, customers, and local authorities.

  • Health, Safety & Environment (HSE): Championing a strong HSE culture, ensuring project activities comply with company policies, CDM regulations, and relevant environmental legislation.

  • Team Leadership & Coordination: Coordinating multi-disciplinary teams (internal staff, consultants, contractors) to foster a collaborative and performance-driven environment.


What you'll need:

Qualifications & Accreditation:

  • A Degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management) or equivalent demonstrable experience.

  • A full Driving Licence is required.

Skills & Experience:

  • Contract Management (NEC Expertise): Demonstrable, in-depth understanding and practical application of the NEC3/NEC4 ECC suite is essential. You must have the ability to interpret contractual requirements and manage contractual processes effectively and fairly.

  • Project Management: Proven ability to manage complex infrastructure projects through the entire lifecycle, with strong planning, organisational, and time management skills.

  • Significant, proven experience managing infrastructure projects, preferably within the utilities, civil engineering, or construction sectors of the water industry.

  • A proven track record of successfully delivering projects on time and within budget.

  • Technical Acumen: Good understanding of civil engineering, M&E, or process principles.

  • Financial Management: Strong budget management, cost control, and financial forecasting skills.

  • HSE Awareness: Strong understanding and commitment to health, safety, and environmental regulations and best practices, including CDM regulations.

  • Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build strong relationships, effectively influence, and negotiate with diverse stakeholders.

Employees are required to be flexible and to be prepared to perform duties and other tasks within their capabilities. The nature of our business is such that the contents of any job profile are subject to change from time to time.

​
Grow a career with a meaningful purpose.

We know the communities we serve are diverse. We recognise creativity comes from diversity not similarity. title: Steward
description:
Our Story

We called ourselves Florida Avenue from the start for our location on one of Tampa's most notable roads. But with time and growth, that name has come to mean more to us and more to our people. We set out in 2010 with a mission to provide a memorable craft beer experience for anyone we met along the way and to represent the Sunshine State to all who walked through our doors. With each beer you enjoy, we want you to taste all this state has to offer, drink it in, and thirst for more. Throughout our state and beyond, we are Florida Avenue.

If you want to kickstart your culinary career, work with a phenomenal team, and enjoy some of the best perks in the industry, you belong here. No previous kitchen experience required!

What You’ll Do

As a Steward, you keep our kitchen running by keeping dish, flatware, and glassware clean, stocked, and ready for service. This entry-level role matters because it protects food safety, supports the line, and keeps the back of house organized during busy shifts.

Responsibilities:
- Wash, sanitize, and rotate dishware, utensils, and glassware throughout service
- Keep dish and cleaning areas clean, safe, and set up for speed
- Assist with deep cleaning and basic upkeep of dish machines and related equipment
- Follow Florida food safety and sanitation regulations at all times

Required:
- Working knowledge of state food safety regulations
- Ability to work mostly nights/weekends and major holidays
- Reliable, team-first attitude and comfort with physical, fast-paced work

Apply to launch your career and grow your skills with a supportive team.

Your Shift, Step by Step

As a Steward, you keep our machine running smoothly. Your day-to-day will be dynamic and goes beyond the dish pit:

  • Dish & Kitchen Care: Maintain cleanliness and organization of the dishwashing area, operating our commercial dish machine, and ensuring cooks and servers have clean tools.

  • Light Culinary Prep: Assist our team during non-peak hours with quick-service portioning and weighing (sauces, cheese curds, wings, etc.).

  • Maintenance & Organization: Take out the trash, conduct line sweeps, help put away orders, rotate back stock, and organize chemical storage areas.

  • Deep Cleaning: Participate in the weekly rotating deep cleaning of various kitchen equipment to keep our back-of-house pristine.

What We're Looking For

  • The Right Attitude: High energy, reliable, and a team-first mindset. You thrive when the kitchen gets busy!

  • Availability: Must be able to work predominantly nights and weekends.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to lift over 50 lbs regularly.

    • Ability to stand on your feet for the duration of your shift.

    • Comfort working in a loud, fast-paced, and wet environment.

Benefits That Matter

Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage
401(k)
Life Insurance
Paid Time Off
Paid Meals
Snack/Drink Room
Employee Discounts

description:

12

Onsite

Seattle University will be one of the most innovative and progressive Jesuit and Catholic universities in the world, educating with excellence at the undergraduate, graduate, and professional levels. We embrace an intersectional framework for defining diversity in its broadest sense, including differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, generational history, culture, socioeconomic class, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, political perspectives, geographic origin and physical ability. Seattle University strives to be a welcome, open and safe campus climate for all who learn, live and work at Seattle University.


Seattle University's Core Competencies


Effective Team Collaboration: Works harmoniously with others towards a common goal, leveraging individual strengths to achieve shared objectives.


Emotionally Intelligent Communication: Engages in a skillful exchange of information, thoughts, and feelings, verbally and non-verbally.


Ethics and Integrity: Demonstrates an unwavering commitment to honesty, professionalism, and alignment with our Jesuit mission in all actions and decisions.


Flexibility and Innovation: Embraces change, approaching problems with curiosity adaptability, and is committed to making a positive impact.


Mindful Inclusion: Fosters mindful inclusion by consciously creating a workplace that celebrates differences, embraces cultural humility, and empowers uniqueness.


Outcomes-Driven Orientation: Sets clear objectives, pursues excellence, and delivers measurable outcomes while upholding Jesuit Catholic values.


Job Description Summary

The Director of Orientation Programs serves as the institutional leader for visioning, strategic direction, and delivery of new student orientation and transition support initiatives for all incoming undergraduate first year and transfer students across the First Hill and South Lake Union campuses. This includes attention to support of traditionally underrepresented student populations and an expansive understanding of the unique onboarding needs of each school or college’s programs at both campus locations. The Director leads the university’s efforts to continuously strengthen and align the path from deposit to matriculation.

Position Description:

The Director of Orientation Programs serves as the institutional leader for visioning, strategic direction, and delivery of new student orientation and transition support initiatives for all incoming undergraduate first year and transfer students across the First Hill and South Lake Union campuses. This includes attention to support of traditionally underrepresented student populations and an expansive understanding of the unique onboarding needs of each school or college’s programs at both campus locations. The Director leads the university’s efforts to continuously strengthen and align the path from deposit to matriculation.

The Director is expected to function in a collaborative manner with a high degree of visibility and contact with students, families, staff, faculty, and administration. This role requires innovation and knowledge of leading-edge practices to enhance the experience of current student populations. In alignment with the university’s commitment to student success, retention, and persistence, the director will use a framework of social justice and Jesuit education to deliver a comprehensive entry-year experience and celebration of key milestones.

Essential Functions:
Strategic Leadership and Vision: 40%

  • Lead university-wide strategy for new student onboarding in alignment with Seattle University’s mission and institutional priorities.
  • Assume responsibility for incoming students post-deposit up to and through the start of their first term.
  • Design, implement, and assess in-person and online new student transition curriculum.
  • Analyze and prepare data and metrics reports and presentations for campus partners and senior leadership in regular cadence leading up to start of each term.
  • Strategize and deliver proactive and reactive responses to student progress through New Student Checklist tasks, with emphasis on high melt risk students.
  • Craft and implement individualized support for unique populations, including but not limited to: Adult learners, BIPOC students, Commuter students, Exchange students, First Generation students, Honors students, International students, LGBTQ+ students, Scholar cohorts, Student Athletes, Transfer students, and Veteran and Military-Connected students.
  • Maintain knowledge of unique onboarding needs for Cornish College of the Arts student experience.
  • Implement behavior-driven anti-melt student and family communications plan to drive completion of essential onboarding tasks on New Student Checklist.
  • Develop strategic plans, goals, and measurable objectives for Orientation Programs.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Fallston, Maryland.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Fallston area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Fallston requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
location: West Orange, New Jersey, United States
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in West Orange, New Jersey.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the West Orange area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near West Orange requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

ADV STERILE COMPOUNDING PHARMACY TECH

SUMMARY:

Under the direct supervision of a pharmacist, assists in the provision of pharmaceutical compounded products to various customers by complying with Federal, State, and U.S. Pharmacopeia requirements. This role is preserved for pharmacy technicians whose primary function is to perform sterile compounding. Practices within the scope of state and federal regulations.

HOURS: You will enjoy three days off a week while working four 10-hour days. No nights or weekends.

Minimum of 5 years of experience as a pharmacy technician required. Minimum of 2 (2) years of sterile compounding experience required. Licensed as a Certified Pharmacy Technician with the Idaho State Board of Pharmacy Pass the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB) Pharmacy Technician Certification Exam or accepted national certification program within 90 days from hire. Completed competencies in sterile compounding, including hazardous compounding. Previous lead experience preferred.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Knows, understands, incorporates, and demonstrates the Organization's Mission, Vision, and Values in behaviors, practices, and decisions. Competent to work in the IV room, including performing high risk/hazardous compounding. Advanced understanding of current USP standards, documentation, and EMR compounding workflows. Provides some functional supervision of technicians. Ensures required departmental functions are completed to provide effective and efficient service. Assists the pharmacist in preparing medications, which includes various material resource management, dispensing, clerical, and billing duties. Precepting duties, as required for new hires and technician students. Mentors technicians in learning new tasks. Strives for and models exactness in following defined sterile procedure and aseptic technique.

Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. Job Description:

Electronics Technician Maintenance II

GDIT is seeking qualified candidates for Electronics Technician Maintenance II in support of the Warfighter Training Readiness Solution (W-TRS) Contract, formally known as ATMP.

W-TRS program purpose is to provide ongoing Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and training-related services in support of U.S. Army training and the U.S. Army SC mission. Services include program management, O&M of Training Aids, Devices, Simulators and Simulations (TADSS) and Government Furnished Property (GFP), TADSS-related services, training services (e.g., individual, crew, unit, and collective training support programs), and logistics services.

GDIT's ETM II Long Bow Training Aircraft Survivability Equipment Simulation Suite (LB TASS) Contact Team (CT) Member will report to the site lead as our Subject Matter Expert (SME) for ensuring Army standard of maintenance for sequential installation, testing, removing and maintaining Threat-Integrated Air Defense Systems (T-IADS) kits and equipment for the Army aviation fleet.

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact as an ETM II. Here, you’ll tailor cutting-edge solutions to the unique requirements of our customer. GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career.

At GDIT, people are our differentiators. As an ETM II you will help ensure today is safe and tomorrow is smarter. Our work depends on a Team Lead joining our team to help build and enable the readiness of our Nation's Army!

HOW WILL AN ELECTRONICS TECHNICIAN MAINTENANCE III MAKE AN IMPACT:

  • Installation, testing, removing and maintaining Threat-Integrated Air Defense Systems (T-IADS) kits and equipment for the Army aviation fleet.

  • Performs routine tasks troubleshooting and repairing military simulators, including using tools and test equipment such as multimeters to diagnose faults. Replace components, wiring circuits, and complex repair functions.

  • Travel (TDY) to numerous locations (CONUS & OCONUS) to support the Army Aviation fleet training.

  • Applies routine technical knowledge and troubleshooting procedures to solve routine problems that typically can be solved by reference to manufacturers’ manuals or similar documents; applies skills in restoring equipment operations.

  • On-site maintenance performed In Accordance With (IAW) technical data; if technical data/checklist is not provided for any single item, maintenance IAW the best commercial standards. Maintain all the documentation (Operator & Maintainer Manual, Instructor/Operator Manual, Commercial Off- The-Shelf Manual, Technical Data Package Schematics and Cold Start Procedures) spares and tools.

  • Captures and records accurate and timely maintenance history ensuring that unique corrective measures for work orders and repair are annotated into the Management Information System (MIS).

  • Reports maintenance issues and general operations updates with supervisor.

  • Maintain all GFP hardware and software IAW technical manuals, including, but not limited to, commercial software installation and Government provided installation (patches, updates).

  • Report on acquisition of supplies, equipment, and parts weekly to site lead.

  • Conduct an inspection and inventory of all assigned equipment before and after each live fire-training event for accountability and serviceability.

  • Supports the required GDIT/W-TRS cross training plan to support other W-TRS TADSS on installation.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

  • Education: AA or 2 years equivalent

  • Required Experience: 2+ years of related experience Maintaining US Army TADSS and/or Military experience preferred

  • Experience using technical manuals, schematics and drawings.

  • Ability to learn the W-TRS Management Information System (MIS) for controls/recording all work orders and Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) property control

  • Required Skills and Abilities: Superb communication skills. Ability to document and report on technical issues and solutions

  • Must be able to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and be able to lift a maximum of 50 lbs.

  • Must be able to obtain/maintain a valid state driver’s license and post driving privileges

  • Must be able to obtain a passport and travel visas for OCNUS travel when requested.

  • Location: On Customer Site and other military reservations

  • Must be able to travel up to 75% of the time.

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE:

  • Comprehensive health and wellness packages

  • Internal mobility team dedicated to helping you own your career

  • Cutting-edge technology you can learn from

Job Description:

Intelligence Trainer

XVIII ABC Hub and Spoke MTCs provide individual and collective training on Army Mission Command Systems, using a variety of tools and Army fielded systems. These systems are used to support Small Unit Training: Squads through Company, Medium Unit Training: Battalion through Brigade, and Large Unit Training: Divisions and Corps in training environments ranging from Stability and Support Operations (SSO) through Unified Land Operations (ULO).

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact as a Intel Trainer at the XVIII Airborne Corps Hub and Spoke Mission Training Complexes (MTC). Here, you’ll tailor cutting-edge solutions to the unique requirements of our customer. GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career.

At GDIT, people are our differentiators. As an Intelligence Trainer, you will help ensure today is safe and tomorrow is smarter.

The Intelligence Trainer serves as a tactical and operational intelligence Subject Matter Expert at the Mission Training Complex (MTC). This role focuses on delivery Intelligence training and exercise support for division and below-level (S2/G2) staff sections. The position requires a flexible, adaptable, and initiative-driven trainer who can independently lead classroom, virtual, and exercise-based training across intelligence disciplines and systems.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT:

  • Deliver in-person and VTC enabled intelligence instruction to groups of up to 20+ or more students across All-Source Intelligence, GEOINT, SIGINT, HUMINT, IMINT, ISR planning, intelligence collection management, and related tradecraft.
  • Independently deliver established curriculum and tailor instruction, practical exercises, and training products to customer requirements, unit missions, and approved training objectives.
  • Develop, update, and refine courseware, including lesson plans, presentations, practical exercises, student materials, intelligence scenarios, and other training products to reflect current doctrine, operational requirements, system changes, and customer feedback.
  • Prepare and maintain classroom, tactical operations center, simulation, and exercise training environments; coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure required resources, systems, and exercise requirements are available and compliant.
  • Design, facilitate, and support individual, collective, staff, command post, warfighter, and operational-rehearsal training events.
  • Develop exercise support products, including intelligence injects, order of battle materials, operational-environment products, threat scenarios, simulation inputs, and other materials required to support the training audience.
  • Perform OPFOR Commander responsibilities, as assigned, to provide realistic threat representation, scenario execution, and intelligence-driven exercise conditions.
  • Operate and train personnel on Maven, AIDP, MUSE, WARSIM Intelligence Model, and other government-directed intelligence or training systems; directly operate systems during exercises as required.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of tactical network connectivity, data feeds, system architectures, and interoperability to support training, system integration, and coordination with technical personnel.
  • Assess student and unit performance against learning objectives and performance standards; provide coaching, feedback, retraining, and recommendations for improvement.
  • Conduct after-action reviews and maintain required training documentation, including attendance records, student assessments, evaluation results, courseware updates, observations, lessons learned, and corrective-action recommendations.
  • Coordinate with military units, installation personnel, government representatives, program managers, and other stakeholders to execute training requirements and deliverables established during training synchronization meetings.
  • Represent the organization in customer meetings, planning conferences, and briefings; mentor instructors, operators, and junior personnel in intelligence tradecraft, instructional delivery, systems use, and exercise-support responsibilities.
  • Maintain current knowledge of intelligence doctrine, tactics, techniques, procedures, systems, emerging technologies, and assigned mission requirements; demonstrate flexibility in response to evolving customer needs, VTC delivery requirements, field conditions, surge periods, and nonstandard work schedules.
  • Perform as a member of the Higher Command (HICOM) response cell during exercise execution answering formal Requests for Information (RFI) from training units.
  • Maintain familiarization with all Command-and-Control Information Systems (C2IS), simulations, stimulations, and gaming systems.
  • Lead/support the development and execution of the site’s internal After-Action Review (AAR) program.
  • Continually assess, innovate, and improve our services to our customers and fully support a comprehensive Quality Control Program (QCP) and Professional Development and Certification Program (PDCP).
  • Work is predominantly intellectual in character and requires the employee to consistently exercise discretion and judgment.
  • Perform limited manual and non-manual work directly related to the general business operations of the Fort Stewart MTC.
  • Participates in special projects and perform other duties as required.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree and 5 yrs or equivalent experience. in lieu of degree.
  • Security Clearance: Top Secret clearance required.
  • Required Technical Skills:
    • Familiarity with Army Command and Control Information Systems (C2IS), Maven Smart System (MSS), and the Intelligence Electronic Warfare Tactical Proficiency Trainer (IEWTPT) system.
    • Understanding of how C2IS systems publish and subscribe to share information.
    • General understanding of the Army simulation and stimulation systems.
    • Familiarity with exercise design and developing Training Support Packages (TSP).
    • Proficiency with Microsoft products to include Word, PowerPoint, Excel and MS Teams; technologically proficient.
  • Required Skills and Abilities:
    • Flexible and adaptable to react to changing requirements and emergent challenges in a fast-paced and high-pressure training environment.
    • The ability to learn and instruct new Intelligence C2IS systems fielded to the military.
    • Strong problem-solving and time management skills
    • Practical knowledge of Collection Management (CM), to include the development of Information Collection Matrices (ICM) and Synchronization Matrices (ICSM).
    • The ability to design and author highly realistic, intelligence-driven Master Scenario Events List (MSEL) injects, script sequences, and simulated message traffic that accurately replicate threat signatures and challenge unit intelligence analysis.
    • The capacity to brief Senior NCOs, Field-Grade Officers (S2s/G2s), and Brigade Commanders with confidence, poise, and professional credibility.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
    • Duties require exercising discretion, independent judgment, and decision-making.
    • Participates in and performs additional duties, special projects, emerging responsibilities as required/directed.
    • Physical labor tasks require the ability to lift/carry 50 pounds and climb ladders to a height of 6 to 12 feet to configure network/power cabling.
  • Location: Fort Stewart MTC. Normal work schedule is 0730-1600, may require night, swing or weekend work shifts depending on specific training event requirements.
  • Travel: May require occasional travel (less than 10%)

description:

All Team Members are treated fairly with dignity and respect.

Team members are required to follow the site specific / brand specific procedures for offering consistent and quality customer experiences.

This location, operated by Convenience Stores Inc- a subsidiary of Jones Petroleum, is looking for a highly skilled, self-motivated individuals looking to assist in our growing Retail Operation.

POSITION SUMMARY

Upholds the Core Values as determined by the management team.

Assistant Store Managers position is responsible for the complete day-to-day operation of the store in the absence of the Store Manager.

Assistant Store Managers are responsible for maximizing store sales and profitability, along with minimizing expenses while ensuring that the store is optimally stocked and merchandised, and to Amaze Every Customer Every Time.

An Assistant Store Manager contributes to the growth and development of the management team and store associates.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (assist in all of the following):

SALES AND OPERATIONS

  • Hire, train and develop store staff with goals for growth and success in their positions, provide ongoing performance feedback, and recognize accomplishments
  • Review all store evaluations with store management team and staff to identify opportunity areas, and correct all issues with a sense of urgency.
  • Coordinate the overall supervision of staff to ensure sales performance goals are met and company procedures are followed accurately.
  • Delegate workload among associates to meet merchandising and visual presentation standards.
  • Participate in associate evaluations as per company standards in order to provide feedback for improvement, praise and recognition, and growth opportunities.
  • Complete merchandising updates according to Jones Petroleum / Convenience Stores Inc. (dba ACE Hardware) standards.
  • Work with vendors to develop merchandising strategies for products and have them assist with their plan-o-gram and updates
  • Forecast scheduling needs to meet customer demand and create work schedules.
  • Monitor payroll to ensure compliance with established budgets and take corrective measures as necessary.
  • Review staffing needs, strengths and opportunities with Store Manager, and/or (where Store Manager is unavailable) District Manager prior to additions, promotions or terminations.
  • Develop and implement an in store marketing strategy including promotions, events, and seasonal merchandising based on store needs.

CUSTOMER SERVICE

  • Promote Customer Service as The #1 Priority. This must be accomplished on a daily basis through observing, monitoring and coaching associate’s performance and interactions on the sales floor.
  • Regularly promote and teach “Amaze Every Customer Every Time” while leading by example and coaching.
  • Use huddles, communication boards, and store meetings as the means to communicate the store’s performance, and educate, engage and motivate the team.
  • Drive customer satisfaction by ensuring that all customers are acknowledged, customer needs are met, and concerns are resolved quickly.
  • Review all customer service measurement reports (e.g., Mystery Shop, Customer Engagement Survey, etc.), and work with the team to identify opportunities in an effort to sustain or improve overall service levels.
  • Document at least one (1) Observation per associate monthly and provide coaching in order to ensure consistency of service to all customers.
  • Job responsibilities may change based on the needs of the business.

INVENTORY

  • Maintain accurate inventory at all stages through on-hand integrity, daily receiving, store communication, product mix and flow, and adhering to Jones Petroleum / Convenience Stores Inc. (dba ACE Hardware) best practices, metrics and deadlines
  • Utilize available inventory reports to reduce shrinkage, maintain appropriate stock levels and maximize inventory accuracy.

COACHING AND TRAINING

  • Work on your professional development through leadership training opportunities (self-directed learning, local business events, Ace learning and industry events, etc.).
  • Identify appropriate training for store associates and oversee all training requirements for all associates (e.g. New-Hire orientation, on-the-job training, vendor training, etc.).

SAFETY, COMPLIANCE AND STORE ENVIRONMENT

  • Enforce safety policies and procedures, and serves as role model for safety.
  • Enforce store environment procedures to ensure and maintain the best store appearance.
  • Conduct preventative safety and fire inspections, and take appropriate actions to correct all issues.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED); or, an equivalent combination of education and experience. Bachelor degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 1 year of leadership experience in a retail or customer service setting.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Must have good verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to provide motivation and leadership to associates storewide in a fair and impartial manner.
  • High degree of analytical skills, and the ability to delegate and be self-directed.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational, time management, and project management skills
  • Technically skilled in basic retail computer systems including related software
  • Develop and maintain client relationships and strategic partnerships
  • Dress according to company policy.
  • Bilingual (Spanish) verbal and written communication skills strongly preferred
  • Possess a valid in-state driver license with an acceptable driving record in accordance with company’s insurance carrier’s standards

Note: This company participates in the E-verify program. This positions is subject to a 90 day introductory period. This introductory period is designed, primarily, to give both the Company and the employee an opportunity to determine whether the employee will be able to adequately perform in the assigned job position. At the end of the introductory period, your performance will be reviewed and a decision made regarding your continued employment or any extended introductory period. All employees are hired as temporary employees until their introductory period has elapsed. Temporary employees are not eligible for any benefits during the introductory period.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Lexington, South Carolina.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Lexington area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Lexington requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Chesterfield, Missouri.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Chesterfield area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Chesterfield requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.
