title: Assistant Dean for Student Affairs
description:
Months Per Year:

12

Work Model:

Onsite

Seattle University will be one of the most innovative and progressive Jesuit and Catholic universities in the world, educating with excellence at the undergraduate, graduate, and professional levels. We embrace an intersectional framework for defining diversity in its broadest sense, including differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, generational history, culture, socioeconomic class, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, political perspectives, geographic origin and physical ability. Seattle University strives to be a welcome, open and safe campus climate for all who learn, live and work at Seattle University.


Seattle University's Core Competencies


Effective Team Collaboration: Works harmoniously with others towards a common goal, leveraging individual strengths to achieve shared objectives.


Emotionally Intelligent Communication: Engages in a skillful exchange of information, thoughts, and feelings, verbally and non-verbally.


Ethics and Integrity: Demonstrates an unwavering commitment to honesty, professionalism, and alignment with our Jesuit mission in all actions and decisions.


Flexibility and Innovation: Embraces change, approaching problems with curiosity adaptability, and is committed to making a positive impact.


Mindful Inclusion: Fosters mindful inclusion by consciously creating a workplace that celebrates differences, embraces cultural humility, and empowers uniqueness.


Outcomes-Driven Orientation: Sets clear objectives, pursues excellence, and delivers measurable outcomes while upholding Jesuit Catholic values.


Job Description Summary

Position Description:

The Assistant Dean for Student Affairs will provide forward-looking, strategic leadership to enhance the academic experience of all undergraduate and graduate students in the College of Arts and Sci ences (CAS). The Assistant Dean will oversee the college’s student support services and carry ou t o ther innovative services to support the academic success, persistence, and development of stude n ts in CAS. More broadly, this position will contribute to the College’s work on the University Strategic Directions and the College of Arts & Sciences strategic plan to improve our inclusive academic excellence.

The Assistant Dean will provide strategic leadership to enhance the recruitment, retention, and lifecycle events of CAS students. The Assistant Dean will carry out strategies, projects, and events across the student experience, from admissions to graduation and beyond. Central responsibilities of this position include increasing and sustaining student enrollment through thoughtful recruitment and yield activities, providing orientation programs for new students and their families, and facilitating lifecycle events and student ceremonies. More broadly, this position will contribute to the University’s Strategic Directions and the College of Arts & Sciences strategic plan to improve our inclusive academic excellence.

Essential Job Functions

Key functions of the role include providing academic and personal guidance to students, consultation to academic department chairs and all CAS faculty, representing the college in committees, board, and policy work, overseeing the academic standing review of CAS students and determining quarterly probation and dismissal decisions, and overseeing student petitions and college decisions regarding degree requirements, registration, and grading.

These functions are carried out in consultation and/or in collaboration with the academic departments and programs in CAS, the CAS Dean and Dean’s office, University Advising, Student Financial Services, Office of the Registrar, University Advancement, University Events, Student Affairs, and other SU colleges and offices. The Assistant Dean reports to the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.

Essential duties include:

  • Represent CAS as Dean’s Designee with the Office of the Registrar on academic forms including Petitions to the Dean and Petitions for Exceptions to Policy, Hardship Withdrawals, Student Leave of Absences, and other relevant review and approval capacities.

  • Oversee quarterly academic standings of all CAS students below the minimum required GPA, making determinations on academic warning, academic probation, and academic suspensions. The Assistant Dean will meet with students on academic suspension and will make determinations on academic reinstatement.

  • Meet with students experiencing academic and personal hardships and assist them in navigating the Hardship Withdrawal process

  • Represent CAS at the Dean of Students office’s weekly CARE team meeting and/or consult with CAS Lead Advisor, reviewing student issues deemed moderate or higher, and planning for appropriate interventions with impacted CAS students.

  • Maintain professional relationships with University Advising and the professional academic advisors in CAS to implement university-wide advising initiatives, polices, and procedures in CAS.

  • Act as primary college contact for university-wide retention efforts and collaborate with Student Affairs, the Provost’s Office, and others.

  • Serve as a primary liaison to University Admissions, regularly providing updates and presentations to University Admissions staff and leadership, and partnering to plan and execute admissions strategies to recruit and yield new CAS undergraduate students.

  • Lead CAS presence at signature University Admissions events, including Fall Preview and Admitted Students Days. Assistant Dean will recruit and coordinate participation of faculty, staff, and students and design the CAS-specific programming.

  • Design and lead additional efforts to augment the recruitment and admissions yield strategies for CAS, including collaboration with the CAS Director of Marketing and Communication, and Seattle University Marketing Communications.

  • Administer CAS Continuing Student Scholarships, including chairing student awards and scholarships review committee and leveraging the Scholarship Universe information system to promote scholarships, facilitate the review of applications, identifying recipients, and disbursing awards.

  • Plan CAS Convening and Induction activities, aligning program with first-year student experience and persistence efforts, and coordinating the involvement and participation of CAS faculty, staff, and students.

  • Administer CAS awards and recognition process, including facilitating the nomination and review process, notifying, and recognizing recipients through various methods.

  • Plan and implement CAS Graduation Celebration, including event set-up, logistics, and coordinating CAS staff and faculty involvement.

  • Provide oversight of Student Executive Council (UG) and Arts and Sciences Graduate Council (GR)

  • Maintain integrity of student records and comply with university policies, deadlines, and procedures related to student enrollment.

  • Serve on CAS and campus-wide committees and working groups.

  • Represent CAS Dean as requested or needed.

  • Respond strategically to evolving university priorities.

Marginal Job Functions

  • ​Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Ph.D., Ed.D., or Master’s degree OR an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the position.

  • Three to five years experience in academic advising administration.

  • Knowledge of appropriate student development theory and a demonstrated capability for personalized and outstanding academic advising practices that contribute to the educational and personal development of students.

  • Demonstrated professional and interpersonal characteristics needed to supervise professional, graduate, and administrative staff, providing developmental leadership and professional growth opportunities in a high-volume and high-pressure setting.

  • Demonstrated capability for collaborative and successful working relationships with diverse stakeholders in an academic environment: faculty, department chairs, program directors, and other academic and administrative staff.

  • Experience with university/college policies and procedures and a demonstrated ability to utilize appropriate judgment in making decisions and recommendations.

  • Expertise in working with students at risk and knowledge of pertinent retention and persistence theory.

  • Effective communication and other interpersonal skills, and the ability to present information in large public venues.

  • Knowledge of program assessment, learning outcomes, and evaluation techniques.

  • Understanding of and appreciation for the role of student services in a Jesuit institution of higher education and a commitment to the university’s mission, vision, and values

  • Demonstrated commitment to diversity and experience working with students of diverse backgrounds.

  • Personal qualities that are essential for this position: professionalism, patience, attention to detail, follow-through, teamwork, calmness, industry, and a sense of humor.

  • Ability to perform duties with minimal supervision.

  • Ability to work regular evening hours and some weekends.

  • This position requires a criminal history background check.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with student data management systems

  • Proficiency in Excel and all Microsoft office software packages

Compensation at a Glance

$91,468 - $93,000


Application Instructions


Please attach a cover letter with your resume when applying. Job postings are open until filled, unless otherwise specified.


Seattle University has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what the University may pay for the position at the time of posting. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as the qualifications of the selected candidate, departmental budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information, and not based on a candidate’s gender or any other protected status.


Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. Seattle University provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your total compensation package.

Benefits at a Glance

Consistent with its fundamental Jesuit values, Seattle University offers a wide range of benefits designed to care for the whole person. Choose from three different medical plans, a dental, and vision insurance programs. Protect your income with life, short & long-term disability coverage. Plan for your future with up to a 10% employer contribution for retirement benefits, comprised of a 5% nonelective employer contribution and an additional dollar-for-dollar match of your voluntary contributions up to a maximum of 5%. You may also take advantage of 100% paid tuition benefits for the employee and dependents, a subsidized transportation benefit, a wellness program with free access to an onsite fitness facility, and a wide variety of campus events. Enjoy a generous holiday schedule, including a paid Holiday break closure in December, vacation and paid sick leave, and paid community service leave. For more information explore the Benefits website at: https://www.seattleu.edu/hr/benefits/

Positions designated as hybrid eligible may offer the opportunity for a hybrid work schedule after successful completion of an introductory period of 3–6 months. In these cases, the role typically begins fully on campus to support onboarding and training, with the potential to transition to a hybrid arrangement thereafter.

Positions designated as on-site are not eligible for hybrid work and are expected to remain fully on campus.

All flexible work arrangements are subject to periodic review and may be modified or discontinued at any time at the university’s discretion.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Littleton, Colorado.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Littleton area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Littleton requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Orchard Park area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Orchard Park requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

Har du spørgsmål til stillingen er du velkommen til at kontakte Retail Knowledge; Kim Aaskov på telefon 21175760.

title: Data Scientist
description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Ontada's Genospace team is transforming precision medicine through advanced analytics, machine learning, and AI-driven insights. We are seeking a Data Scientist to help turn complex healthcare, genomic, and clinical data into actionable insights that support research, clinical development, and patient care.

In this role, you will apply machine learning, statistical modeling, and generative AI techniques to develop predictive models, build analytical solutions, and deliver data-driven recommendations. You'll collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, clinicians, and scientists to advance precision medicine solutions used by leading healthcare organizations.

What You'll Do (Responsibilities)

  • Analyze and validate healthcare, clinical, and genomic data to support research and business decisions.
  • Build, test, and deploy machine learning models that generate actionable insights.
  • Develop AI and large language model (LLM) solutions using prompt engineering techniques.
  • Perform statistical analyses and translate findings into clear recommendations.
  • Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations for technical and business audiences.
  • Partner with product, engineering, clinical, and scientific teams to solve complex data challenges.
  • Write production-ready code and support multiple analytics initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

Basic Requirements

  • Master’s degree with 2+ years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent experience.
  • Relevant experience in Data Science, Machine Learning, Analytics, Statistics, or a related field.
  • Strong experience programming with Python or R and writing complex queries using SQL.
  • Experience applying statistical techniques to analyze data and generate insights.
  • Experience creating data visualizations, dashboards, or analytical reports and developing or supporting machine learning models.

Preferred Skills/Experience

  • Master's or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience developing machine learning models using techniques such as NLP, deep learning, Random Forests, or Gradient Boosting.
  • Hands-on experience with Generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and prompt engineering.

title: Seniorspecialist, Brand
description:
Vil du være med til at styrke Jyske Banks brandposition – og omsætte forretning, kundeindsigter og data til skarpe strategier, solide koncepter og kommunikation, der virker?

Om jobbet

Som Seniorspecialist bliver du en central del af Brand i Jyske Bank.

Du kommer til at arbejde på tværs af hele den brandstrategiske proces – fra brand- og kundeanalyser til at omsætte koncern- og forretningsstrategi til brand- og marketingplaner, kreative briefs, koncepter og kampagner. Du får en drivende rolle i vores brandprojekter og ansvar for at strukturere og drive projekter fremad i tæt samarbejde med forretningen, kolleger i Kommunikation & Marketing og eksterne bureauer hele vejen fra problemstilling og retning til implementering og opfølgning.

Dine ansvarsområder

Du kommer blandt andet til at:

  • omsætte Jyske Banks brandposition, koncern- og forretningsstrategi til relevante brand- og marketinginitiativer og kampagner
  • drive større og komplekse projekter og kampagner på tværs af forretningen, interne fagligheder og eksterne samarbejdspartnere
  • udvikle målgruppeindsigter, kvalificere værditilbud og omsætte dem til strategisk retning, kreative briefs og koncepter
  • analysere brandperformance og omsætte brandtracking, kundeindsigter og andre datakilder til klare indsigter, anbefalinger og forretningsrapportering
  • sætte mål og succeskriterier og følge op på effekten af vores indsatser
  • udvikle præsentationer og beslutningsoplæg, der gør komplekse problemstillinger enkle, intuitive og levende.

Om dig

Du er strategisk dygtig, tænker kommercielt – og samtidig typen, der får ting til at ske.

Du kan forstå en forretningsmæssig udfordring, se hvad der er vigtigt for kunden og omsætte det til en klar brand- og marketingmæssig retning. Du har et godt analytisk blik og kan bruge data og indsigter til at kvalificere anbefalinger, prioriteter og kampagner – med fokus på, hvad der skaber værdi for forretningen og virker i markedet.

Du har samtidig blik for den kreative side af branding og forstår, hvordan en god indsigt og en skarp brief kan skabe et godt afsæt for kreative løsninger. Du kan se forskel på en god idé og den rigtige idé – og være med til at kvalificere de koncepter, der bedst løser opgaven.

Vi forestiller os derfor, at du har solid erfaring med strategisk brandarbejde og kampagner, der virker – fra bureau eller en større marketing- eller brandorganisation – og er vant til selvstændigt at tage ansvar for strategiske opgaver og projekter, skabe retning, fremdrift og samarbejde på tværs af fagligheder.

Du har solid erfaring med følgende områder:

  • brandstrategi, positionering og strategisk marketing
  • omsætning af forretningsstrategi og kommercielle behov til brand- og marketingindsatser
  • brand- og kundeanalyser samt kvalitative og kvantitative data
  • udvikling af målgruppeindsigter og value propositions
  • kreative briefs, koncept- og kampagneudvikling
  • brand- og marketingplanlægning
  • projekt- og procesledelse i større organisationer
  • strategiske præsentationer og beslutningsoplæg.

Du forstår både de kreative processer og virkeligheden i en større organisation og kan derfor bygge bro mellem forretning, brand- og marketingstrategi og kreativ udvikling og eksekvering.

Sådan arbejder du

Du er nysgerrig og går aktivt efter at forstå den reelle problemstilling, før du springer til løsningen. Du involverer de rigtige mennesker, lytter til forskellige perspektiver og udfordrer konstruktivt, når det gør løsningen bedre.

Du arbejder struktureret, skaber fremdrift og følger tingene til dørs. Du kommunikerer klart, tager ansvar og er åben for feedback undervejs.

Og så kombinerer du høj faglighed og ambitioner med en uhøjtidelig tilgang. Vi har en kultur, hvor vi gerne vil sætte barren højt – med et smil, der smitter.

Om os

Brand sætter retning for Jyske Banks brandposition og arbejder for, at banken fremstår tydelig, sammenhængende og nærværende over for kunder, medarbejdere og omverden.

Vi arbejder blandt andet med positionering og brandplatform, brand- og kundeindsigter, værditilbud, større brand- og kampagnekoncepter, brandtracking samt Jyske Banks visuelle identitet og fysiske brandeksekvering.

Brand er en del af Kommunikation & Marketing, og vi er 50 kolleger inden for brand, kommunikation, marketing og digitalt salg. Vi arbejder tæt sammen – både internt i enheden, med forretningen og med eksterne samarbejdspartnere.

Praktisk

Du bliver en del af Brand-teamet og refererer til afdelingsdirektør for Brand, Trine Møgelvang.

Stillingen kan have base i Silkeborg eller København. Har du base i København, skal du forvente arbejdsdage i Silkeborg typisk 1-3 gange om måneden.

Ansøgningsfrist

Vi oplever mangfoldighed som en styrke – både i opgaveløsningen og i fællesskabet. Derfor opfordrer vi alle til at søge, og vi glæder os til at høre fra dig.

Vi behandler de indkomne ansøgninger løbende og forventer at holde samtaler i løbet af oktober. Vi tager opslaget ned, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat. Rekrutteringsprocessen varetages i samarbejde med Senior HR Business Partner, Birgitte Schøler.

Hør mere om jobbet

Hvis du har spørgsmål til jobbet, er du velkommen til at kontakte afdelingsdirektør for Brand, Trine Møgelvang på tlf. 20461418.

title: Membership Coordinator Lekki
description:

The Membership Coordinator is a passionate leader who ensures that guests who come to church are managed, retained, and assimilated into Harvesters' culture and vision, while actively contributing to HICC's five strategic objectives:
  • Church Planting
  • Leadership Development
  • Health and Growth
  • Reach and Transformation

2. Leadership Development

  • Recruit and coordinate volunteers to create additional social opportunities that help build relationships with new converts.

  • Provide weekly updates to the Church, departmental team and Pastor on membership growth and attendance trends.
  • Follow up with members regularly, attend to their needs and address complaints and disputes.
  • Communicate regularly on progress towards membership development objectives and outcomes.

  • Develop and implement strategies that help guests feel at home and develop a strong sense of belonging to Harvesters.

  • Meet the welfare and benevolence needs of members within the church's established financial processes.

  • Minimum qualification: First degree OR a diploma/certificate from a recognized Bible college.

  • A committed born-again Christian with a personal and active relationship with God.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
location: Long Valley, New Jersey, United States
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Long Valley, New Jersey.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Long Valley area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Long Valley requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team

title: Data Engineer
description:
Job Description

Role Summary

The Data Engineer designs, builds, and operates the ingestion, transformation, and Lakehouse solutions that power Masco's enterprise POS and adjacent commercial data. This role delivers high-quality, reliable, and secure data pipelines against the standards and specifications set by the Enterprise Data Architect and the direction of the Data Engineering Leader. The engineer contributes across the full pipeline lifecycle — ingestion, data quality, transformation, and enrichment — including the pipeline-side execution of the enterprise attribution crosswalk. Depending on assignment, the Data Engineer may focus more heavily on ingestion or on quality and pipeline development, but the role covers all aspects.

What You'll Own

Ingestion & Pipeline Development

  • Design, build, and maintain automated ingestion pipelines and multi-source integration for retailer, HQ, and BU data on the Databricks and Azure data stack.

  • Develop RESTful APIs and API-based integrations for retailer and third-party data acquisition.

  • Deliver critical-path pipelines and validation for priority data feeds.

  • Integrate with orchestration tools and cloud or hybrid storage systems to enable end-to-end data workflows.

  • Contribute to Lakehouse solutions using ACID-compliant storage layers, schema enforcement, and versioning for reliable data management.

Data Quality, Validation & Monitoring

  • Run data-quality checks at the pipeline level — missing values, outliers, consistency, and cross-source reconciliation.

  • Implement monitoring, validation, and automated notifications within the data lifecycle to protect performance, quality, and availability.

  • Support pipeline monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement in partnership with the Data Engineering Leader.

  • Maintain change control and testing processes for modifications to pipelines and data models.

Attribution & Master Data Support

  • Build the ingestion side of the attribution crosswalk and master data foundations against the Enterprise Data Architect's documented spec.

  • Support maintenance of hierarchy mappings and attribute relationships through pipeline work.

  • Surface data-quality issues, mapping exceptions, and structural gaps back to the Data Engineering Leader and Architect.

DevOps, Automation & Data Preparation

  • Implement CI/CD pipelines for data engineering workflows and automate testing, deployment, and monitoring of data solutions.

  • Develop, maintain, and secure tables, relationships, metrics, and calculations for analytical models supporting reporting and advanced analytics.

  • Contribute to research and recommendations on data management products, services, and standards.

Documentation & Knowledge Management

  • Document ingestion patterns, pipelines, validation rules, and metric definitions as part of the definition of done.

  • Contribute pipeline lineage and technical metadata to the enterprise catalog.

  • Follow the documentation standards established by the Data Engineering Leader and Enterprise Data Architect.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field; equivalent professional experience considered.

  • Substantial hands-on experience designing and building data engineering solutions on a major cloud platform, with emphasis on the Azure ecosystem.

  • Experience delivering production pipelines and supporting them in an operational setting.

Technical Skills

  • Advanced hands-on expertise with Databricks and the Azure data stack (Data Factory, Data Lake, Synapse, Analysis Services).

  • Strong working knowledge of the medallion architecture (bronze / silver / gold) for structuring Lakehouse solutions.

  • Familiarity with Microsoft Fabric and how it fits alongside Databricks in a modern enterprise data platform.

  • Advanced SQL / T-SQL (queries, stored procedures, functions, indexes, partitions, DDL, DML) and strong ETL/ELT design and build experience.

  • Strong proficiency in Python (or Scala) for data engineering.

  • Experience with RESTful API development for data acquisition and ingestion from retailer and third-party sources.

  • Working knowledge of distributed processing (Apache Spark) and Lakehouse principles — ACID storage, schema enforcement, versioning.

  • Solid understanding of CI/CD, DevOps, and automation for data workflows.

  • Strong understanding of Kimball dimensional modeling, including snapshot/transactional fact tables and conforming dimensions.

  • Working knowledge of data constructs including keys, constraints, data types, normalization, referential integrity, and data quality analysis.

  • Understanding of data governance, security, and compliance as they apply to data engineering.

Skills & Competencies

  • Detail-oriented and thorough. Considers all aspects of a data problem, including how the small pieces relate to the larger picture.

  • Highly self-motivated and self-directed. Operates with minimal oversight on complex, hands-on data work.

  • Delivery-focused. Owns commitments and follows through.

  • Willingness to explore and understand new and modern data tools to add value to the enterprise POS and POS-related engineering space.

  • Collaborative with the Data Engineering Leader, Enterprise Data Architect, and BI Developers on shared pipelines, models, and metric definitions.

  • Continuous learner who stays current on modern data engineering practices and tools.

  • Strong communicator who can explain technical detail clearly to both engineering and analytics peers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in retail, consumer goods, or manufacturing analytics environments where POS, sell-in, inventory, and third-party retail data are core.

  • Experience with Databricks Unity Catalog, data lineage, and observability tools.

  • Familiarity with ML/AI integration (MLflow, Azure ML) and DataOps/MLOps practices.

  • Experience with Microsoft Tabular models and the DAX language.

  • Experience with at least one data analysis tool such as Power BI, Tableau, etc.

title: Private Lacrosse Coach
description:
Coach lacrosse on your own schedule in Greenville, South Carolina.

STXZ Lacrosse has 1 opening(s) for independent lacrosse coaches in the Greenville area, to cover client requests for private lessons we can't currently fill. We bring you the clients. You run the sessions.

About STXZ

STXZ is a technology platform that connects families with independent lacrosse coaches across the United States. We send you clients in your area, handle the administrative work, and get out of your way so you can coach. If you have lacrosse experience and want coaching work on a flexible schedule, this is for you.

How it works

When a family near Greenville requests lessons through STXZ, we send you a client offer with the details. You review it and decide whether to take it. No quotas, no pressure, no penalty for declining.

When you accept:

  • You contact the client directly within 24 hours
  • You and the client agree on schedule and location: their home, a local field, a park, your call
  • You run the session your way. Drills, pacing, and structure are your professional judgment
  • You submit a quick lesson briefing on the platform after the session
  • You get paid

STXZ never tells you how to coach, what drills to use, or how to structure your lessons.

What you earn

  • $35 to $50 per one-hour session, paid as a flat per-lesson rate. Rates are set by STXZ, vary by market and demand, and are confirmed in writing before your first lesson.
  • Payout within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your lesson briefing, via PayPal
  • 1099-NEC issued at year end if you earn $2,000 or more through the platform
  • Paid per completed session. Lesson volume depends on client demand in your area, and STXZ does not guarantee a minimum number of lessons.
  • No fee to apply, and nothing to pay up front

Schedule

Most lessons run weekday afternoons and evenings and on weekends. Work when you want and pause your availability anytime.

What you control

  • Your schedule. Accept or decline every offer without penalty or impact on your standing.
  • Your methods. Drills, lesson plans, teaching style, all yours.
  • Your territory. Set your own travel radius, from a few miles to 35 or more.
  • Your approach. You decide what equipment to bring to each session.

What STXZ handles

  • Client acquisition. We market the platform and bring families to you.
  • Matching. We send you local client offers that fit your profile.
  • Payment processing. We collect from clients and pay you after each session.
  • Billing, refunds, and disputes. Our support team handles all of it. You coach.
  • Liability coverage. Active coaches are enrolled in STXZ's platform liability coverage program for sessions booked through STXZ. The program fee is $30 per year, and it is $0 down: nothing is due to get started or to begin receiving client offers. The fee is recovered from your first lesson payout once you start coaching. This is limited coverage for platform-booked sessions only; independent coaches may also choose to carry their own personal insurance.

Who this is for

  • Coaching experience at the youth, high school, club, or college level, or playing experience at the high school varsity, club, college, or professional level
  • 18 or older
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States
  • Willing to complete a third-party background check, arranged by STXZ, before receiving full client details
  • Reliable transportation to training locations in your area
  • Your own stick and basic training equipment: cones, balls, training aids
  • Strong communication with parents, players, and the STXZ team
  • Professionalism and confidence working independently with families and youth athletes

How to apply

Apply here (about 2 minutes). If your background fits, we send a short coaching profile questionnaire: playing history, coaching experience, positions, availability. After review and background screening, approved coaches start receiving local client offers.

STXZ is a technology platform that connects clients with independent lacrosse coaches. STXZ does not employ, supervise, manage, or control coaches or their training sessions. Coaches are engaged as independent contractors and are responsible for their own coaching methods, taxes, and scheduling. STXZ considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

title: SUPERSELGER I EN 70% STILLING PÅ ONLY STORO
description:
Vil du bli med på reisen?

​

ONLY Stores er i sterk utvikling, og vi søker derfor en ambisiøs superselger som kan bidra til en utvikling av vår butikk på ONLY STORO.

​

Bli en del av ONLY Stores

ONLY Stores har vært på en forrykende reise gjennom de siste fem år, og vi er langt fra ferdige med reisen. Vår forretningsplan har vist seg å være riktig. Vi har hatt vårt primærfokus på to ting – våre produkter og våre medarbeidere. Som en del av organisasjonen i ONLY Stores kan du i høy grad få det ansvaret du ønsker, de oppgaver du brenner for, og ikke minst være en del av et fantastisk team.

Hos ONLY Stores vet vi at våre medarbeidere gjør en stor forskjell!

​

Jobben

Som 70% selger hos oss så forventer vi at du kjenner deg igjen i verdiene våre, er glad i et høyt tempo hvor ingen dag er lik og ønsker å være en del av og en bidragsyter til teamet ditt. Mote og trender er noe som interesserer deg og du er opptatt av å følge med i markedet.

Har du høyt tempo, konkurranseinstinkt, og du er klar for å ta i et tak! Er du en team player som kan bidra til et godt arbeidsmiljø og jobbe sammen med teamet for å nå målene vi setter oss? Mener du også at kunden alltid kommer først? Da vil vi høre fra deg!

Stillingen vil innebære dag, kveld og helger, men vi har også behov for at du kan stille opp ekstra ved sykdom, varetelling og ferieavvikling.

Vi gleder oss til å høre fra deg!

Konkret vil dine arbeidsoppgaver innebære:

  • Jobbe med egne nøkkeltall daglig
  • Merchandising
  • Oppgjør
  • Varetelling
  • Ansvar for butikken/personale når butikkleder er på ferie/syk

Din profil

Du kjenner retailbransjen innenfra og du har en naturlig interesse for mote. Du er en person med høy grad av energi, har sans for detaljer, og du tør å sette retningen. Det er viktig at du er utadvendt i din arbeidsstil , og du er i stand til å skape et solid nettverk. Du er god på og skape team og øke kompetansen til de rundt deg.

​

Vi gleder oss til å høre fra deg!

​

Om oss

ONLY Stores er en del av BESTSELLER Retail Europe vi har eksisteret i mer enn 25 år og driver konseptbutikker under følgende brands: ONLY, ONLY & SONS & JDY.

Vi har base i Brande, hvor vi er 40 dedikerede kollegaer, som beskjeftiger oss med drift av butikker. Vi driver BESTSELLER Retail Europe ut fra ledelsesmessige verdier, som bygger på fremgang for enhver pris, nærhet til våre kollegaer og butikker og en uskuelig tro på, at vi kan gjøre det enda bedre i morgen.

Vi arbeider i et sterkt konkurransemessig miljø, hvor vår innsats og innstilling gir resultater direkte på bunnlinjen. Vi hyller prinsippet om frihet under ansvar, og vi elsker mennesker som tar initiativ og som gjør en forskjell. Vi tror på, at det er den måte vi best utvikler vår forretning og hverandre.

  • Advance avian developmental biology and embryology / uncover the basis of skin appendage patterning / translate animal-model insights to morphogenesis and evolution / collaborate in the innovative TREE Lab

  • Apply now to drive impactful developmental biology research and accelerate your postdoctoral career in a leading science faculty.

  • Investing in you – 17% superannuation, benefits package including salary packaging, health and wellbeing programs, discounted services, and professional development opportunities.

The University of Melbourne
We take pride in our people, who all contribute to our mission to benefit society through the transformative impact of education and research. Discover more via our website.

Your next career opportunity
You will lead experimental embryology and skin biology projects that manipulate avian and vertebrate developmental programs.

You will apply advanced imaging, genome editing and functional genomics to reveal how genes sculpt morphology.

You will also build your research profile through publications, grants and supervision within a supportive, high performing lab.

What you will deliver:

  • Design and execute in vivo functional assays and genetic perturbations in avian and other vertebrate embryos.

  • Perform and interpret functional genomics and imaging experiments to uncover mechanisms of skin appendage development.

  • Develop and maintain embryonic and primary cell culture models to investigate gene regulatory networks and morphogenesis.

  • Prepare ethics and OGTR applications, reports, and high-impact publications, contributing to grant proposals and lab strategy.

  • Mentor students and junior researchers, and present findings to academic, industry and public audiences.

You may be a great fit if you:

  • Hold a PhD in developmental biology, genetics, or related discipline, with strong postdoctoral research experience.

  • Bring substantial hands-on expertise in vertebrate embryology, especially mouse, zebrafish or avian models, and in vivo assays.

  • Demonstrate proficiency in functional genomics, including experimental design, tissue handling and data analysis.

  • Maintain and manipulate primary and established cell culture lines, integrating molecular, cellular and tissue-level approaches.

  • Publish in high-quality journals, prepare manuscripts and reports, and contribute to competitive grant and ethics applications.

  • Thrive in collaborative, multidisciplinary environments, engaging productively with industry, clinical or institute-based partners and stakeholders.

For further information please refer to the attached PD.

What we offer you!
We offer the opportunity to be part of a vibrant community and enjoy a comprehensive range of benefits to support your success and sense of fulfilment, including:

  • Build future financial security with 17% superannuation

  • Supportive flexible work arrangements underpinned by our commitment to inclusion and well-being

  • Career development opportunities, including access to a range of tailored programs, such as Academic Women in Leadership, and learning platforms including LinkedIn Learning

  • Progressive, considerate leave provisions to empower your work-life balance and well-being, including leading parental leave, gender affirmation leave and cultural leave

  • Salary packaging and access to a range of discounted services including Bupa health insurance, and access to unique cultural and recreational benefits such as discounts for the Melbourne Theatre Company

  • Health and well-being services including a leading Employee Assistance Program

For more information check out our benefits page!

Your new team – School of BioSciences

Based in the School of BioSciences, you will join the Trait Reconstruction Engineering and Experimentation Lab. The Lab explores how genomes shape body plans and skin appendages across diverse vertebrates. You will collaborate with developmental biologists, geneticists and evolutionary scientists across the Faculty of Science. The team offers strong technical support, access to advanced imaging and genomics platforms, and mentoring for research independence.

Reporting to the Executive Director of Career Engagement, the Associate Director translates the university’s institutional employer engagement strategy into coordinated outreach, partnership development, recruiting activity, and measurable student opportunities. The position manages the full lifecycle of employer engagement from prospect identification and relationship cultivation through activation, stewardship, assessment, and renewal.

The Associate Director works closely with Career Engagement colleagues, the Albers Career Center, faculty, experiential learning partners, Alumni Engagement, Advancement, Student Employment, and other campus stakeholders to support an integrated university-wide career ecosystem.

The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to Seattle University’s Jesuit Catholic mission, professional formation, social justice, equity, inclusion, cultural humility, and student success.

Essential Functions

Employer and Industry Partnership Development - 35%

  • Develop and maintain a diverse portfolio of employer, industry, government, nonprofit, and community partnerships aligned with student interests, academic programs, workforce trends, and institutional priorities.
  • Identify and cultivate new employers that can provide internships, entry-level employment, project-based learning, mentorship, job-shadowing, career treks, classroom engagement, and other experiential opportunities.
  • Build employer pipelines across industries and occupational areas, with particular attention to sectors with strong regional demand and relevance to Seattle University students.
  • Meet with employers to understand workforce needs and develop customized engagement strategies that connect organizations with Seattle University students, faculty, academic programs, and university initiatives.
  • Advise employers on recruiting practices, internship program development, employer branding, campus visibility, and inclusive approaches to attracting and retaining early-career talent.
  • Proactively cultivate organizations committed to creating equitable access to employment and experiential learning for first-generation students, students of color, students with disabilities, international students, veterans, and other historically underrepresented populations.
  • Maintain awareness of labor-market conditions, emerging industries, workforce trends, recruiting practices, and changing employer expectations.
  • Represent Seattle University and Career Engagement at employer meetings, professional associations, chambers of commerce, workforce-development conferences, and community events.

Employer Stewardship and Partnership Activation - 20%

  • Manage the full employer relationship lifecycle, including cultivation, onboarding, activation, stewardship, assessment, renewal, and expansion.
  • Develop engagement plans for priority employers and ensure consistent communication and follow-through across the university.
  • Translate employer interest into specific opportunities such as internships, jobs, mentoring relationships, sponsored projects, career events, classroom presentations, site visits, and experiential learning partnerships.
  • Coordinate with academic colleges and campus partners to connect employer opportunities with appropriate students, programs, faculty, and student organizations.
  • Support college-based career and professional formation leaders by providing access to employer relationships, labor-market insights, and external partnership opportunities.
  • Strengthen employer retention by providing responsive service, gathering feedback, communicating impact, and identifying opportunities for deeper engagement.
  • Develop resources and engagement pathways that make it easier for employers to understand how to connect with Seattle University.

Recruiting and Career-Connected Programming - 25%

  • Provide strategic and operational leadership for employer-facing recruiting programs and career-connected events.
  • Collaborate with the Career Education team to ensure that employer programming complements students’ career readiness preparation and learning needs.
  • Partner with the Albers Career Center and other university offices to coordinate employer outreach, reduce duplication, and create a consistent experience for employer partners.
  • Recruit employers and industry professionals to participate in mock interviews, résumé reviews, mentorship programs, classroom presentations, career education workshops, and other student-learning activities.
  • Support the development of micro-internships, project-based experiences, job-shadowing, and other lower-barrier opportunities for students who are still developing professional experience.
  • Ensure that employer programs and recruiting activities comply with university policies, applicable employment regulations, ethical recruiting standards, and National Association of Colleges and Employers guidance.

Institutional Collaboration and Experiential Learning - 10%

  • Serve as an employer-facing resource for university initiatives related to internships, experiential learning, mentorship, workforce development, AI career readiness, and professional formation.
  • Help identify gaps in experiential opportunity by academic program, student population, career interest, and industry.
  • Support the development of scalable practices for connecting academic learning with employer-sponsored projects, internships, research, service, and other applied experiences.
  • Participate in cross-campus committees and working groups related to employer engagement, experiential learning, student outcomes, and workforce readiness.
  • Ensure employer engagement efforts complement specialized career services within the Albers School of Business and avoid unnecessary duplication.

Data, Systems, Assessment, and Reporting - 10%

  • Establish measurable goals for employer outreach, partnership development, opportunity creation, employer retention, and student engagement.
  • Maintain accurate employer relationship, recruiting, and opportunity data within Handshake and other approved university systems.
  • Develop dashboards, reports, and summaries that communicate employer engagement activity and impact to Career Engagement leadership and university stakeholders.
  • Assess employer satisfaction and use feedback to continuously improve services, programs, and partnership practices.
  • Monitor internships, jobs, recruiting activity, employer participation, and other indicators of partnership effectiveness.
  • Collaborate with Career Engagement colleagues to connect employer engagement data with student participation and post-graduation outcomes.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, higher education, human resources, communications, marketing, public relations, nonprofit leadership, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • At least five years of progressively responsible experience in employer relations, university recruiting, talent acquisition, business development, workforce development, corporate relations, alumni relations, career services, or a related field.
  • Experience translating relationships into programs, opportunities, partnerships, or measurable outcomes.
  • Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, presentation, and relationship-management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple partnerships, projects, events, deadlines, and priorities.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across organizational boundaries and with stakeholders who have varied goals and responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, social justice, cultural humility, and serving diverse student populations.
  • Ability to use data and technology to manage relationships, assess performance, and inform decisions.
  • Availability for occasional evening or weekend programs and local travel to employer and community sites.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a college or university career center, employer-relations operation, talent acquisition function, workforce-development organization, or corporate partnership role.
  • Knowledge of university recruiting, internship development, experiential learning, mentorship, early-career hiring, and employer engagement practices.
  • Familiarity with customer relationship management systems, career-services technology, or employer relationship-management platforms.
  • Experience using labor-market information and employer data to guide strategy.
  • Familiarity with National Association of Colleges and Employers standards, career-readiness competencies, and ethical recruiting principles.
  • Understanding of the Seattle and Puget Sound employer, nonprofit, government, and workforce-development landscape.
  • Experience supporting fundraising, sponsorship, corporate engagement, or partnership models that include financial and nonfinancial investment.

Seattle University Mission Alignment

The Associate Director advances Seattle University’s mission of educating the whole person, promoting professional formation, and empowering leaders for a just and humane world. By connecting students with meaningful work, professional relationships, experiential learning, and organizations committed to positive social and economic impact, the position helps students translate their education into lives of purpose, leadership, and service.

The Associate Director will ensure that employer engagement reflects Seattle University’s Jesuit values and expands access to social capital, professional networks, and career opportunities for all students.

Compensation at a Glance

$67,000 - $74,700


Application Instructions


Please attach a cover letter with your resume when applying. Job postings are open until filled, unless otherwise specified.


Seattle University has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what the University may pay for the position at the time of posting. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as the qualifications of the selected candidate, departmental budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information, and not based on a candidate’s gender or any other protected status.


Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. Seattle University provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your total compensation package.

Benefits at a Glance

Consistent with its fundamental Jesuit values, Seattle University offers a wide range of benefits designed to care for the whole person. Choose from three different medical plans, a dental, and vision insurance programs. Protect your income with life, short & long-term disability coverage. Plan for your future with up to a 10% employer contribution for retirement benefits, comprised of a 5% nonelective employer contribution and an additional dollar-for-dollar match of your voluntary contributions up to a maximum of 5%. You may also take advantage of 100% paid tuition benefits for the employee and dependents, a subsidized transportation benefit, a wellness program with free access to an onsite fitness facility, and a wide variety of campus events. Enjoy a generous holiday schedule, including a paid Holiday break closure in December, vacation and paid sick leave, and paid community service leave. For more information explore the Benefits website at: https://www.seattleu.edu/hr/benefits/

Positions designated as hybrid eligible may offer the opportunity for a hybrid work schedule after successful completion of an introductory period of 3–6 months. In these cases, the role typically begins fully on campus to support onboarding and training, with the potential to transition to a hybrid arrangement thereafter.

Positions designated as on-site are not eligible for hybrid work and are expected to remain fully on campus.

All flexible work arrangements are subject to periodic review and may be modified or discontinued at any time at the university’s discretion.

title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Job Description:

Are you a hands-on worker and a problem-solver who likes working independently? Do you enjoy meeting new people and travelling to new places? Have you been seeking a long-term career but keep hitting a dead end?

Look no further than Modern Pest Services! Pest management is a pandemic- and recession-proof industry where you’ll make a meaningful difference in the health and safety of your community while maintaining independence and ownership over your own work.

What You'll Do:

Modern Pest is seeking a Pest Control Technician to service our clients in North Conway, NH and the surrounding towns/cities. In this role, you'll spend your day on the road solving pest challenges, building long-term relationships with your clients, and protecting homes and businesses from dangerous, destructive, and disease-carrying pests.

At Modern Pest, we value hardworking individuals with a strong customer service mindset, and welcome those seeking a new opportunity, a career change, a supportive team with growth opportunities, and a management team that sets you up for success.

How You'll Spend Your Day:

  • Upon successful completion of our paid training and onboarding program, you'll have earned your state-specific pesticide applicator's licenses and be ready to work independently.

  • Each morning, you’ll drive straight to your first client’s home or business to begin your day, traveling to and from client locations in your company-owned vehicle along a pre-scheduled route as your day goes on.

  • At each stop on your schedule, you’ll spend time building and maintaining client relationships, assessing the true extent of the infestation or pest-related damage, customizing and executing an effective and safe treatment plan, and offering education and preventative measures to avoid future pest issues.

  • With new challenges and puzzles to solve every day, you’ll utilize your critical thinking and expertise to ensure that our communities remain safe, sanitary, and healthy.

  • By conducting thorough interior and exterior inspections to monitor pest activity, you'll offer both immediate and preventative pest management plans to solve the issue long-term.

  • As the pest control expert, you'll offer advice and education to clients on both chemical and natural pest control remediation options.

  • You'll safely administer pest control measures, including spraying perimeters of homes and structures for termites, ants, and other insects, or using bait or traps to eliminate rodent infestations.

  • By getting to know our clients and their homes/businesses, you'll be able to recommend products and services for long-term, effective pest control, such as our eco-friendly, all-digital SMART solutions.

What Kind of Pests can I Expect to Encounter?

Here at Modern, we'll train you to protect our communities against common household pests including, but not limited to:

  • Ants

  • Flies

  • Bees/wasps

  • Cockroaches

  • Pantry pests

  • Fleas

  • Rodents

  • Ticks

  • Mosquitos

Details You'll Want to Know:

  • Job Type: Full-time, year-round, benefit eligible.

  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, with rotating Saturdays as needed.

  • Branch Location: This position will report directly to the Manchester Branch located in Chichester, NH. Orientation and training will be conducted at the Chichester location.

  • Work Location: This position requires travel in a company vehicle to our clients based in North Conway, NH and the surrounding towns and cities. To reduce unnecessary drive time and be as efficient as possible, following completion of Orientation and training, your route will be scheduled within a reasonable driving distance from North Conway, NH.

  • Pay: Hourly pay rates start at $20 with transferable experience or skills. Higher rates are available for candidates with industry or similar experience!

What Do I Need to Get Started?

Required Experience, Education, and Skills:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required

  • Valid driver’s license required; must meet minimum age requirement of 21 years and/or possess a minimum of 3 years' driving experience for insurance coverage purposes

  • Must consent to driving company-owned vehicle equipped with front, internal, and rear dash cams; continuous recording is required by our insurance during operating hours for safety, liability protection, and driver training.

  • Proof of vaccination may be required to service certain client accounts.

  • Must pass all required state licensing exams to meet minimum qualifications by the completion of paid training.

  • Must meet minimum conduct and attendance standards during 90-day Introductory Period.

What Screenings are Required for this Role?

  • Clear 7-year background screen

  • Clear 3-year Motor Vehicle Report (MVR)

  • 4-panel drug screen (opioids, cocaine, PCP, and amphetamines)

What Benefits does Modern Offer?

Health and Wellbeing:

  • Benefits are easy as 3, 2, 1! Select from 3 Medical plans, 2 Dental plans, and 1 Vision plan through the Horizon and Delta networks

  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) for medical and childcare expenses

  • HSA with employer match (for qualifying plans)

  • 100% company-paid Life Insurance and Short Term Disability plans

  • Voluntary Life Insurance, Long Term Disability, Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity insurance options

  • Employee Assistance Programs at no additional cost

Financial Peace of Mind:

  • Competitive hourly compensation

  • Company vehicle and gas card

  • Company cell phone

  • 401(k) Savings with company match

  • Employee referral bonus program

  • A peer-to-peer employee recognition bonus program

Work/Life Balance:

  • Full time, year-round employment

  • Paid training and in-depth orientation

  • 2 weeks of Paid Time Off and 8 Annual Paid Holidays in the first year of employment

  • Employer-provided uniforms

  • Advancement opportunities within both Modern Pest and our parent company, Anticimex

title: DevOps / Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Tuleva tiimisi odottaa!

61N on nopeasti kasvava puolustus- ja turvallisuustoimialan tietojärjestelmiä kehittävä vahvasti tamperelainennoin 70hengen konsulttitalo. Toteutamme päätoimittajana kokonaisturvallisuuden kannalta kriittisiä tietojärjestelmiä. Projekteissamme näet konkreettisesti työsi vaikuttavuuden yhteiskunnan turvallisuudelle. Olemme profiloituneet toteuttamaan vaativia järjestelmäkokonaisuuksia ja toimimme useissa projekteissa myösintegraattorinaohjaten muiden toimittajien työtä. Henkilöstömme koostuu kokeneista ohjelmisto- ja tietojärjestelmäalan ammattilaisista, joilla on vahvaa osaamista erityisesti turvallisuus- ja puolustustoimialan toimintaympäristöistä.

Olemme teknologia-agnostisia ja valitsemme parhaat teknologiat kuhunkin käyttötarpeeseen, huomioiden tietojärjestelmän koko elinkaaren. Meille infrastruktuuri ei ole vain palvelimia ja verkkoja, vaan toimiva ja hallittu kokonaisuus, jonka varaan asiakkaan palvelut rakentuvat.

Roolisi meillä

Etsimme joukkoomme kokenutta DevOps / Site Reliability Engineeriä starttaamaan 61N:n uuden palvelutuotantotiimin, jolla on halu huolehtia siitä, että asiakkaidemme järjestelmät toimivat luotettavasti ja turvallisesti.

Tehtävässäsi tuet eri asiakasprojektitiimejä ja niiden tuotantoympäristöjä sekä kehität 61N:n omaa infraa. Huolehdit ympäristöjen ylläpidosta, valvonnasta, häiriötilanteiden selvittämisestä, automatisoinnista ja jatkuvasta kehittämisestä. Haluat ymmärtää, miksi järjestelmä toimii tai ei toimi, etkä tyydy vain korjaamaan yksittäistä oiretta. Osallistut myös uusien ympäristöjen rakentamiseen ja käyttöönottoon silloin, kun se on tarpeen. Tässä tehtävässä sinulla on mahdollisuus kehittää yhteisiä toimintatapoja sekä ympäristöjen valvontaan ja hallintaan käytettäviä menetelmiä. Yksin hommaa ei tietysti tarvitse tehdä, vaan tukenasi ovat muut rautaiset ammattilaisemme. Työskentelemme tiiviisti myös asiakkaiden kanssa, joten teknisen osaamisen lisäksi arvostamme hyvää yhteistyö- ja palveluasennetta.

Toimintaympäristömme ovat usein hybridimuotoisia: julkipilveä voidaan yhdistää asiakkaan omiin, turvaluokiteltuihin on-premise-ympäristöihin. Siksi tehtävässä korostuvat teknisen osaamisen lisäksi huolellisuus, dokumentointi, tietoturva ja kyky ymmärtää kokonaisuuksia.

Mitä odotamme sinulta

Lopullinen rooli muotoutuu tekijänsä mukaan, mutta odotamme sinulta osaamistaseuraavista:

  • Ohjelmistokehityksen koko elinkaari mm.versionhallinta, julkaiseminen ja testaus ovat sinulle tuttua
  • CI/CD-putkienjascriptientekemisestä
  • DevOps-työkalut(esimerkiksiGitlab,Ansible,Terraform)
  • Erilaiset järjestelmävalvonta- ja hälytystyökalut (esimerkiksi Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Grafana Alloy, Prometheus)
  • Toimiminen erilaisissa ympäristöissä(esim.Linux,Kubernetes,Openshift, k3s) joko pilvessä (AWS,Azure) ja/tai on-premises-ympäristöissä
  • Asiakaslähtöistä palveluasennetta

Kokemus ja osaaminen seuraavista on eduksesi, muttei pakollista:

  • Palvelunhallinnan ja –tuotannon kokemusta
  • Tekoälyn hyödyntämisestä palvelutuotannon tukena

Huomioithan myös, että vaikkakintyöskentelemme joustavastihybrid-mallissa,projektiemme luonteen ja yhteisöllisenkulttuurin vuoksiodotamme,että olet valmis työskentelemään osan viikostatoimistollamme Tampereella. Lisäksi projektimme vaativat tällä hetkellä ammatillista ja sujuvaa suomen kielitaitoa jatyösuhteen ehtonaonhyväksytty viranomaisen turvallisuusselvitys(ja toisinaan huumausainetesti). Otathan huomioon, että työtehtävä sisältää varallaoloa, joka tarkoittaa ajoittaista ilta- ja viikonlopputyötä.

Tarjoamme sinulle työn, jossa merkityksellisyys on arkipäivää

Meidän projekteissamme olet mukana rakentamassa kansallista turvallisuutta –yhteiskunnan tärkeimpiä digitaalisia ratkaisuja. Voimme luvata, että meillä työn merkityksellisyys on läsnä arjessasi!Liittymällä tiimiimme saat myös mahdollisuuden tulla mukaan rakentamaan uutta menestystarinaa–olemme hyvin mielenkiintoisessa kasvuvaiheessa, ja meillä pääset todella vaikuttamaan. Lisäksi tarjoamme:

  • Kilpailukykyisen palkan, joka tämän roolin puitteissa on4900-6500e/kkosaamisestasi ja kokemustaustastasi riippuen
  • Kattavat ja monipuoliset henkilöstöedutmukaan lukienlaaja työterveysja tapaturmavakuutus,liikunta- ja kulttuurietu, lounasetu, yrityksen puhelinliittymä ja koti-laajakaista sekä modernit valitsemasi työvälineet
  • Tuemme tekijöidemme ammatillista kehittymistäyhdessä sovituilla tavoilla, aina mentoroinnista koulutuksiin ja sertifioinneista valmennuksiin
  • Mukavan ja motivoituneen työkulttuurin, jossa tukea on saatavillaja voit vaikuttaa kasvuyrityksen matkaan

Job Description:

Keep growth on track and your career in motion as a Senior Subcontracts Administrator Growth Lead at GDIT. Your work supporting strategic capture and proposal efforts will power business growth, competitive positioning, and long‑term mission success for our customers.

As a Senior Subcontracts Administrator Growth Lead dedicated to proposal and capture management, the work you’ll do at GDIT will directly shape our ability to win new business. In this role you will lead all subcontract‑related tasks across the capture lifecycle, ensure compliance with federal acquisition regulations, develop competitive sourcing strategies, and surface risks early by driving cross‑functional alignment with capture, pricing, contracts, and technical teams.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT

  • Reports directly to the Growth Strategist as an integral member of the team, supporting execution of sourcing strategies and subcontract management activities

  • Lead subcontractor engagement and sourcing strategy during capture and proposal development, including developing requests for proposals (RFPs), evaluating supplier capabilities, and leading competitive analysis. Ensure compliance with FAR/DFARS requirements and GDIT policies

  • Coordinate all subcontract‑related inputs for proposals, including cost/price data, teaming documentation, non-disclosure execution, compliance artifacts, and technical volume contributions when required. Ensure small business and socioeconomic considerations are incorporated

  • Analyze capture requirements and identify subcontracting risks, gaps, and opportunities; recommend mitigation strategies to the Capture Manager and Proposal Manager. Escalate risk concerns leadership when applicable

  • Utilize artificial intelligence to identify potential gaps or risks between subcontractor agreements and customer requirements

  • Prepare and deliver subcontractor status updates, risk assessments, and pricing insights to leadership and capturing stakeholders

  • Support continuous improvement across the proposal subcontracting process by identifying inefficiencies and recommending enhancements to templates, workflows, and subcontractor engagement models

  • Utilize GDIT’s source‑to‑pay and proposal systems to track subcontractor activities, ensure documentation completeness, and provide accurate data for color team reviews and leadership briefings

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED
Bring your acquisition expertise along with a drive for growth and competitive excellence to GDIT. The Senior Subcontracts Administrator Growth Lead must have:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in business, contracts, supply chain, government acquisition, or related business field; 4 years of additional experience may be substituted in lieu of degree.

  • Experience: 5+ years supporting federal subcontracting, procurement, or proposal development, with strong familiarity in FAR‑based environments

  • Technical skills: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite

  • Role requirements:

    • Experience developing RFX’s to suppliers, analyzing subcontractor proposals, negotiating agreements or terms, working in source‑to‑pay or contract management systems

    • Strong understanding of subcontracting processes throughout capture and proposal phases, including price analysis, competitive sourcing, and compliance considerations

    • Ability to identify risks, troubleshoot issues, and proactively elevate challenges to capture and procurement leadership

    • Ability to clearly communicate with internal teams, external partners, and executive leadership

  • Location: This is a hybrid position working at our GDIT facility in Falls Church, VA. Must be comfortable working onsite (3) days a week minimum.

  • U.S. Persons required

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE

At GDIT, the mission is our purpose, and our people are at the center of everything we do.

  • Growth: AI-powered career tool that identifies career steps and learning opportunities

  • Support: An internal mobility team focused on helping you achieve your career goals

  • Rewards: Comprehensive benefits and wellness packages, 401K with company match, competitive pay and paid time off

  • Community: Award-winning culture of innovation and a military-friendly workplace

OWN YOUR OPPORTUNITY

Explore a career in supply chain and logistics at GDIT and you’ll find endless opportunities to grow alongside colleagues who thrive on efficiency, accuracy, and accountability.

The likely salary range for this position is $81,349 - $89,999. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

Scheduled Weekly Hours:

40

Travel Required:

10-25%

Telecommuting Options:

Hybrid
